description: spec/matching.md section 17: the form of the three result fields after the fifteen of v5 (SECURELOCK-HARDENING-SPEC.md 13.4), field 15 landedAt, field 16 ranUntil and field 17 slClass, as the trustedzones write them and PoxMatching, the validators' members and the runners read them. A result that carries them is version v6 (field 0 `v6`); a v5 result carries the fifteen fields and no more. PoxMatching's decoder does not read field 0. Each field is the whole of its bytes between its colons, written as plain unsigned decimal: "0", or a digit 1 to 9 followed by digits 0 to 9, with no prefix or label, sign, space or leading zero; landedAt and ranUntil at most 2^64 - 1, slClass 0 (the custom class) or 1 (the default class). A result whose three fields are not all in that form, or that has fewer than eighteen fields, carries none of them: it has no class, and noteAmbiguous refuses it (NotAmbiguous reason 4). The eighteenth colon ends field 17; what follows it is not read. accepted: results whose three fields are read, with the values decoded; refused: results whose fields are not read, with the first field that fails (null when fewer than eighteen fields) and its test, empty, leadingZero, notDigit or aboveMax in that order (absent for fewer than eighteen fields); each with the stored result a node adds. stored: the vectors of the stored result's own grammar, v3:0x<lower-case hex of the signed transaction>[:<rest>] (storedGrammar): the forms that carry a transaction and the forms that carry none, each with what the grammar reads from it.
base: result-v5.json examples.plain.result with field 0 replaced by the version (v6 when `after` holds a field, v5 when it holds none) and field 1 by the task code, then the fields of `after` each after a colon

versions.v5: the fifteen fields of result-v5.json and no more
versions.v6: the fifteen fields of v5 followed by landedAt, ranUntil and slClass, fields 15 to 17; fields after field 17 are not read

transaction.note: privateKey is keccak256 of keyLabel, `to` the last 20 bytes of keccak256 of toLabel; the stored result is v3:<the signed transaction, 0x hex>:<cid>, the transaction calling _addResultToOrder(orderId, result)

storedGrammar.description: spec/matching.md section 17, "The stored result": the one grammar of the string a node adds with _addResultToOrder, the form both trustedzones write into transaction.txt and the node agent copies between v3: and the result's CID. PoxMatching's decoder and the validators' members read it by this rule, byte for byte: nothing is trimmed or skipped.

otherSigner.note: the key of the vector other-signer, keccak256 of keyLabel

transaction: the hex run, from after 0x to the next colon or the end of the string, is the transaction: at most maxTransactionBytes bytes
one RLP list that is all of the bytes, of nine items none of which is a list: nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, v, r, s

canonical RLP: a length below 56 in the short form, from 56 on in the long form with no leading zero byte, and a single byte below 0x80 written as itself, never as a one-byte string (0x81 and the byte)
to is empty or 20 bytes; v, r and s are read as big-endian integers of at most 8, 32 and 32 bytes
v is 27 or 28, or 35 and above (EIP-155: chain id (v - 35) / 2, parity (v - 35) % 2); s is at most half the order of secp256k1
the signature recovers a signer over keccak256 of the RLP list of items 0 to 5 as their bytes stand, followed for EIP-155 by the chain id, an empty item and an empty item

data is exactly the selector of _addResultToOrder(uint256,string), the order id (below 2^64), the offset 0x40, the string's length and its bytes padded with zero bytes to a whole word; the string is valid UTF-8

statuses.decoded: a transaction for the order, whose result string holds a run of digits in field 1: the task code (PoxMatching decoder status 0)
statuses.notV3: the string does not begin v3: (status 3: NodeFaultRefused reason 3; for notRun a result with no enclave transaction)
statuses.noTransaction: the string begins v3: and is outside the grammar (status 4: NodeFaultRefused reason 4; for notRun a result with no enclave transaction)
statuses.otherOrder: a transaction that calls for another order (status 5: NodeFaultRefused reason 5)
statuses.noCode: a transaction for the order whose result string has no run of digits in field 1 (status 8: NodeFaultRefused reason 4)

storedGrammar.vectors: stored: each vector's name, the form of its bytes, the stored result and what the grammar reads from it for the fixture's order id: status, transaction (whether the bytes carry a transaction: every status but notV3 and noTransaction), and for a transaction its order id and signer, with the task code when decoded. The result string is the plain result with task code 39 unless the form says otherwise; the transaction's fields are the fixture's unless the form names another (chain id 0 for v 27 or 28, a nonce, a value, another key).

v6.rule: a v6 result is one whose field 0 is v6; fields 0 to 14 are v5's with field 13 in the ten-value form below. PoxMatching reads fields 1 and 15 to 17 from a result of eighteen fields or more and nothing after field 17. The round's writers write twenty fields: 15 landedAt, 16 ranUntil, 17 slClass, 18 closeBlock, 19 closeRows, every one plain decimal. Positions 20 and 21 are reserved for the first and last block of a relay wait in a later version.

fieldMeaning.closeBlock: a block at which the DO request's row count is at least closeRows: the final input sweep's closing read; for a transferred or forced session the window's toBlock; 0 only with closeRows 0
fieldMeaning.closeRows: the enclave's row cursor over all metadata rows of the DO request when its input side ended; 0 without a session

readers.agent: code and ESR fields read as v5; no class

readers.poxMatching: fields 15 to 17 read; nothing after field 17
readers.members: fields 18 and 19 read by readClosingPosition after the signer is established

v6.sessionOrderRule: a DO request is a session request when its metadata3, fixed at the add, begins v3s:; field 11 must agree with it (0f on another request, a session status on a session request); a result that disagrees is an invalid form, not a ban cause

membersChecks.rule: closeBlock above the block the result landed in (orderResultAt, read for every judged order): invalid session; closeRows above the request's row count at the judged block: invalid session; a lower bound that needs a read at an older block (statuses 1 to 3, 6, 7) that does not answer: retried, never a verdict; closeRows below the lower bound: invalid session, a node fault (inputs withheld), a ban cause on the terms of an input mismatch; the input root over the first closeRows rows, by the row grammar of session-rows.json, differing from field 7: invalid session, a ban cause. A result with no closing position decides neither a ban nor an invalid verdict from its input side. An input-side mismatch is a ban cause only for rows at or below the network's landing depth (session_landed_depth_blocks); the rows a session reads, of every key, are bounded at 1,024: a flood ends the session as status 4 (flooded), a dApp fault, never charged to the node.

lowerBounds.closed: the position of the order's first close row in the request's row list, plus one
lowerBounds.complete-at-timeout, expired-idle, expir: the row count at the first block whose timestamp reaches the input cutoff (the time the enclave's loop ends: securelockCloseAt, or the input cutoff after which rows are answered with late notices)
lowerBounds.flooded: the position of the row that met the bound, plus one
lowerBounds.unsupported-securelock: as closed or complete-at-timeout by how the session ended
lowerBounds.transferred, transfer-forced: the row count at the window's toBlock

v6.enclaveRules: the closing block is read before any pump of the final sweep, and when the count at it is below the cursor (a lagging replica answered the earlier pump) the head is read again until it is not; no row at or past the count at closeBlock is consumed; a final sweep that gets no closing read, or does not read to the count at its closing block, ends the order SESSION_RELAY_FAULT (39), never a stated short cursor or a block 0; input rows are read at the network's landing depth

field13.rule: field 13 is etny-cu-delivered-gflops=<gflops>|<n0>|<t0>|<t1>|<validator>|<sig t0>|<sig t1>|<block0>|<block1>|<salt> in the round's writers: ten values, the salt the tenth, sig t1 over the statement with nonce = closeNonce(n0, salt, "<gflops>"); a reader tells it from the nine-value form of before (result-v5.json probed, both statements over n0) by its value count, not by the version word. On a network whose pricing names a PoxMatching a nine-value field 13 is no probe (no strike, no admission); elsewhere it is a probe as at 52e36e0. The rate bound applies with W = probeRounds x the node's record's cuworkers x opsPerRound (capability-record.json rateBound).

vectors.name: ten-values-window-too-long
vectors.rule: a window of 12 s bounds the probe at 230 GFLOPS: 240 is refused (it passes at 52e36e0)
